maria: quick follow-up on the probabilistic eviction budgeting experiment i spun up this morning. TL;DR: sampling-based soft-demote reduced token egress in the Dedicated cluster by ~12% in the 2h run but introduced a small uptick in tail read latency for a handful of tenants. details below.

devon: thanks for running this. can you summarize how the budgeting decision is made? is it per-prefix or per-tenant?

maria: per-tenant budget, applied at prefix granularity. we sample prefix accesses with a cheap reservoir sketch and estimate hotness. eviction decision is probabilistic so we avoid large coordinated demotes during spikes. pseudocode:

maria: ```
# sample-driven cheap estimator
for access in incoming_stream:
    sketch.add(access.prefix, access.weight)

# periodic adjudicator
for tenant in tenants:
    budget = tenant_budget[tenant]  # tokens/sec equivalent
    hot_prefixes = sketch.top_k(tenant, k=budget_scale)
    for p in tenant.prefixes:
        p.prob_demote = clamp(1 - hot_rank(p)/budget, 0, 1)
        if random() < p.prob_demote and !p.soft_pinned:
            mark_soft_demote(p)
```

sam: interesting. my main worry is correctness: demote must never violate read-after-write guarantees for recently-written prefixes. how do we prevent races with handoffs?

maria: good call. current safeguard: we check prefix.leased_epoch and prefix.last_write_ts. we only allow probabilistic demote if last_write_ts < now - demote_grace_ms and leased_epoch == current_epoch (so no mid-handoff demotes). edge case: if handoff is in-flight but epoch hasn't advanced yet. possible fix is to require a handshake flag from the ownership service.

jen: were any client-visible errors observed?

maria: no errors surfaced in the app tier, but we saw an increase in 99.9 P95 read-after-write revalidation in the runtime telemetry for 3 tenants (small ones with bursty writes). hypothesis: sampling undershot a few hot prefixes and demoted them briefly, causing extra readback to origin.

devon: can we quantify the tradeoff? cost savings vs extra origin reads?

maria: yes. numbers from the run: 12% net token egress savings, origin request count +4% for affected tenants, tail latency for reads +8ms median and +30ms at 99.9 for those tenants. broader fleet unaffected.

sam: that seems promising but we need a safety net. suggestion: add a hard pin window for recently written prefixes (e.g., 60s) and keep a small LRU of recently-demoted prefixes to auto-rehydrate without going to origin immediately. also emit a metric that counts demote->origin read transitions.

maria: noted. current config uses demote_grace_ms=30000. i'll try moving to 60000 and add a short-lived rehydrate cache (soft_rehydrate_ttl=15s) to absorb flaps.

jen: also add per-tenant rate-limits: if a tenant's origin-reads spike by >X% post-demote, throttle demote probability for that tenant.

devon: agree. we should also guard the demote decision with ownership fence: require prefix.ownership_state == STABLE for demote. that prevents demote during handoffs.

maria: good point. implementation detail: ownership_state check will need a fast local cache to avoid adding RPCs on hot path. we can rely on the existing epoch metadata replicated to the runtime.

sam: can you share the logs snippet that showed the demote events?

maria: pasted below (sanitized):

maria: ```
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] [prefetcher] demote: prefix=abc123 tenant=team-f evict_type=probabilistic sample=0.021 hot_rank=72 budget=50 leased_epoch=42 last_write=2026-03-15T10:11:22Z
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] [rehydrate] miss->origin: prefix=abc123 tenant=team-f latency=85ms
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] [prefetcher] demote: prefix=def999 tenant=team-x evict_type=probabilistic sample=0.003 hot_rank=501 budget=40 leased_epoch=40 last_write=2026-03-15T09:50:00Z
```

devon: curious about the sample values; are they calibrated per-tenant? small tenants will have noisy samples. maybe use a Bayesian shrinkage to avoid overconfident demotes for low-signal tenants.

maria: yep, currently we apply a min_sample_count threshold before allowing demotes and a smoothing factor toward global mean. tuning followup planned.

jen: operational checklist before wider rollout:
- add metric: demote_triggered, demote_confidence, demote_to_origin_count (per-tenant)
- enforcement: require ownership_state==STABLE and last_write < demote_grace_ms
- safety throttle: if origin_reads increase > 5% in 5m window, reduce demote probability by 2x for that tenant
- instrumentation: sample stack traces for origin reads to ensure they're read-paths and not reconfigs

maria: will implement those. also adding a canary: start with 1% of hosts in canary pool but only for multi-tenant nodes (no single-tenant Dedicated pools).

sam: one more thought: when demote probability is >0.9 we basically want a full demote; when it's 0.1 it's a nudge. maybe expose the prob value in our logs/telemetry so we can correlate actual random outcomes with metrics.

maria: done — will log prob value and random draw. example: `demote_prob=0.12 draw=0.07 -> demote=true`.

devon: for correctness proofs, we should document the invariant: "no demote can happen if prefix has a write with timestamp >= last_stable_epoch_checkpoint". match that to ownership fencing semantics and add a unit test that simulates an in-flight handoff plus demote tick.

maria: adding test plan:
- unit: ownership_state transitions + demote check
- integration: simulated handoff while probabilistic demote runs (fuzz random seeds)
- chaos: canary with induced epoch flips

jen: timeline?

maria: i'll open a follow-up PR with metrics + ownership_state guard today. want to run another 6h canary with demote_grace_ms=60000 and soft_rehydrate_ttl=15s tomorrow morning.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled -> group=prob-evict-canary hosts=canary-1..canary-5 start=2026-03-16T08:00:00Z :rocket:

sam: excellent. please post the dashboard link when it's up and pin the alert rules for demote_to_origin_count per-tenant. :thumbsup:
